title: Sign of the first extension of an injective resolution
statement: Let C be an abelian category with Ext groups and let R be an injective resolution [def-sp-injective-resolutions] of G. Suppose S=(G→R⁰→Z¹(R)) is the short exact first row, with its augmentation and canonical map to cycles. In Mathlib’s Ext and mapping-cone conventions [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the cocycle iCycles:Z¹(R)→R¹ satisfies R.extMk(iCycles)=−S.extClass in Ext¹(Z¹(R),G).

source.place: Tags 06XR (lemma-compute-ext-resolutions) and 06XV (lemma-ext-1); agent-written cone-homotopy sign verification for Mathlib.

proof.text: Place S in cochain degree zero. Its cone quotient q:Cone(G[0]→R⁰[0])→Z¹(R)[0] is a quasi-isomorphism. Let z be the cycles inclusion viewed as a map to the shifted resolution. The cone boundary is minus the first projection in Mathlib.

source.place: Tags 06XR (lemma-compute-ext-resolutions) and 06XV (lemma-ext-1); agent-written cone-homotopy sign verification for Mathlib.

proof.text: Construct a cone homotopy from q followed by z to the negative cone boundary followed by the shifted augmentation. Take the homotopy to be zero on the suspended G summand and minus identity R⁰ on the R⁰ summand, transported through the extension-by-zero and shift coordinate isomorphisms. In degree zero the identity is cancellation of the two augmentations; in the other component it is the factorization d⁰=toCycles≫iCycles. All other degrees vanish. The mappingCone.descHomotopy constructor verifies exactly these two component identities.

source.place: Tags 06XR (lemma-compute-ext-resolutions) and 06XV (lemma-ext-1); agent-written cone-homotopy sign verification for Mathlib.

proof.text: Apply the derived localization to the homotopy. The map q and the resolution augmentation become isomorphisms. Cancel them, use the definition of extMk and the cone roof defining S.extClass, and use naturality of localization’s shift comparison. The resulting equality is extMk(iCycles)=−S.extClass.
